A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FaST research work. Their complete 28-page contents, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–F, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original preferred-response prediction and personalized-generation experiments on DnD and ELIP, including quantitative comparisons, ablations and additional appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and outcomes in Section 4 and Appendix D, including the prediction accuracies and generation evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same feature discovery, probability-weighted feature scoring, FaRM weight learning and iterative sampling-and-tuning procedures. No method component or objective changes.

E1.justification: Both evaluate prediction and personalized generation on the same English datasets: DnD with 129 situations and 10 characters, and ELIP with 100 questions and eight user profiles. No additional domain, population or test scenario appears.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 2 and 4 and the appendix comparisons. Both retain CPM, RM and RM-LoRA for prediction, and the same in-context learning, SFT/DPO, RM-based and oracle generation methods.

E3.justification: Both retain the 50%/25%/25% data splits, model backbones, accuracy and generation metrics, training settings and Elo evaluation design. The smaller-model and LoRA experiments were already present in v1.

E4.justification: Training-size robustness analyses in Figures 2–3, FaRM ablations in Table 12, the LoRA comparison in Table 17 and user examples with learned feature weights in Tables 19–20 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report five random splits for prediction and three for generation. Appendix D.3 retains the checks across three judgment runs and averaging over 25 match-order shuffles. No uncertainty-reporting or significance-testing practice changes.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results, curves, rankings and generated examples are unchanged, including the appendices. For example, Table 2 reports Phi-4-Mini-based FaRM test accuracies of 69.4% on DnD and 75.3% on ELIP in both versions.

T1.justification: The likelihood objective and reward definitions in Equations 1–2, Appendix A's convexity proof and the mathematical definitions of the ablation variants remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: PPALLI, the DnD and ELIP datasets, feature-based FaST alignment from limited data, competitive personalization and potential benefits for under-represented users.

C2.justification: The interpretations of overfitting, robustness and user-specific results are unchanged. Both retain limitations concerning candidate-response diversity, LLM-judge evaluation and simplified ELIP user preferences.

D1.justification: Footnote 2 replaces v1's promise of a future code-and-data release with a statement of public availability and the repository address github.com/naver/fast. This adds concrete access information; implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware disclosures and appendix prompts are unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 45 cited works and research positioning are retained, including the relationship to compositional preference models, personalized alignment and alignment from limited data.

P1.justification: v2 adds Universitat Pompeu Fabra to Germán Kruszewski's affiliations, renumbers affiliation markers, updates version/date text and rewrites the availability footnote. The scientific prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The affiliation update and longer availability footnote produce limited layout changes, including text reflow on pages 2–3 and small line-break changes elsewhere. All three figures and 26 tables retain their content, structure and placement.

improvement.justification: The concrete code-and-data link in v2 replaces a future-release promise, making the paper's reproducibility information more actionable. Scientific evidence and limitations remain unchanged, so the improvement is limited. The supplied PDFs do not establish the linked repository's completeness or usability.
